Can cause fetal harm - avoid; use contraception
No starting-dose adjustment; little data in severe impairment

summary: Temsirolimus is an intravenous inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) used to treat advanced renal cell carcinoma. It is given as a 25 mg IV infusion once weekly with antihistamine premedication to reduce hypersensitivity/infusion reactions. Characteristic metabolic effects are hyperglycaemia and hyperlipidaemia (hypertriglyceridaemia/hypercholesterolaemia), and it can cause interstitial lung disease (ILD/pneumonitis), myelosuppression, infections, bowel perforation and impaired wound healing. Dose reduction is required in hepatic impairment, and strong CYP3A inhibitors/inducers materially alter exposure.
indications: Treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma

dosage.d: 25 mg IV infused over 30-60 minutes once weekly
dosage.n: Premedicate with IV diphenhydramine ~25-50 mg about 30 min before each dose

dosage.d: Reduce by 5 mg/week steps to a minimum of 15 mg/week for significant toxicities
dosage.n: Hold/modify for ANC <1000, platelets <75,000 or grade-3+ toxicity
Return to 25 mg after stopping the inhibitor (washout ~1 week)
Return to 25 mg after stopping the inducer

admin: Premedicate with an IV antihistamine (e.g. diphenhydramine) ~30 minutes before each infusion to reduce hypersensitivity/infusion reactions
Dilute per protocol and infuse over 30-60 minutes using an in-line filter and non-DEHP/non-PVC infusion set
Monitor during and after the infusion; slow or interrupt for reactions and restart at a reduced rate after recovery
Use within the recommended time after preparation; protect from excessive light
Do not give live vaccines during treatment
moa: Temsirolimus and its active metabolite sirolimus bind the intracellular protein FKBP-12; this complex inhibits the serine-threonine kinase mTOR. mTOR inhibition blocks signalling that controls cell-cycle progression and reduces levels of hypoxia-inducible factors (HIF-1/2) and VEGF, producing antiangiogenic and antiproliferative effects in tumour cells.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to temsirolimus, sirolimus, polysorbate 80 or excipients
Bilirubin >1.5x ULN (moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment) - increased risk of death
relative: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (require dose modification/avoidance)
Recent or planned surgery (impaired wound healing)
monitor: Complete blood count and liver function tests
Signs of infection and wound healing

preg: Temsirolimus can cause fetal harm based on its mechanism and animal findings. Women of childbearing potential should avoid pregnancy and use effective contraception during and for a period after treatment; men with female partners should also use contraception. Avoid use in pregnancy.
lact: It is not known whether temsirolimus is excreted in human milk; because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding should be discontinued during treatment.
renal: No starting-dose adjustment is recommended for renal impairment, and temsirolimus is not appreciably removed by dialysis; data in severe renal impairment are limited, so use with caution.
hepatic: Hepatic impairment increases exposure and toxicity. Reduce the starting dose in mild impairment (e.g. to 15 mg/week); it is contraindicated/should be avoided with bilirubin >1.5x ULN (moderate-to-severe impairment) due to an increased risk of death. Monitor liver function.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, grapefruit) - markedly raise sirolimus exposure; avoid or reduce dose
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - lower exposure; avoid or increase dose
Live vaccines - avoid (impaired immune response/infection risk)
moderate: ACE inhibitors / calcium-channel blockers - increased risk of angioedema with mTOR inhibitors
minor: Drugs affecting glucose or lipids may compound metabolic effects
interactions.food: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition); the IV diluent contains alcohol.
interactions.alcohol: The supplied diluent contains alcohol; avoid additional alcohol and counsel patients accordingly.
interactions.diagnostics: Raises blood glucose, triglycerides and cholesterol; can lower blood counts and raise liver enzymes/creatinine - monitor these laboratories.

serious: Interstitial lung disease (pneumonitis), which may be fatal
Serious infections (including opportunistic) due to immunosuppression
Intracerebral haemorrhage in patients with CNS tumours on anticoagulation
emergency: Signs of bowel perforation (severe abdominal pain, fever)

monitoring: Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile before and periodically during treatment
Complete blood count (often weekly) and liver function tests
Pulmonary symptoms and chest imaging for suspected ILD
Signs of infection and wound healing; hypersensitivity during infusions
counsel: This is a weekly IV infusion; you will receive an antihistamine first to reduce reactions
Tell staff immediately of flushing, breathlessness, chest tightness or rash during the infusion
Report a new or worsening cough or shortness of breath, as this can signal a lung problem
Your blood sugar and cholesterol may rise - you may need extra monitoring or treatment
Avoid grapefruit, live vaccines and people with infections; use effective contraception
pk: Pharmacologic mTOR inhibition occurs promptly after the IV infusion
Peak plasma concentration at the end of the infusion
Temsirolimus half-life ~17 hours; active metabolite sirolimus ~55 hours
Store vials refrigerated and protect from light; use prepared infusion within the labelled time
pearls: Always premedicate with an IV antihistamine to reduce hypersensitivity/infusion reactions
Expect and monitor hyperglycaemia and hyperlipidaemia - check fasting glucose and lipids
Watch for interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis - investigate any new respiratory symptoms
Contraindicated with bilirubin >1.5x ULN (increased mortality); reduce dose in mild hepatic impairment
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers require dose reduction/increase; avoid grapefruit and live vaccines
missed: Temsirolimus is given weekly in a clinic; if a scheduled infusion is missed, contact the treatment centre to reschedule. The treating team will adjust timing - patients should not attempt to self-administer or double up.
overdose: There is no specific antidote; the maximum tolerated dose is not established. Overdose may intensify toxicities (myelosuppression, metabolic, pulmonary). Manage with supportive care and close monitoring; temsirolimus is not appreciably removed by dialysis.
